name: the Aruvi
identity: Forest woodwrights and grove-tenders who carve lanterns from living wood and share their villages with spirits.
architecture: Houses grown rather than built: living-willow walls, rope bridges between great trees, lacquered shrines among the roots, and moth-lanterns on every branch.

festivals.name: Moth Lantern Night
festivals.description: Everyone releases a paper lantern with a wish carved on its frame, and the moths follow them up into the canopy.

festivals.name: the Tending
festivals.description: Each village brings gifts to its grove's patron spirit and asks, very politely, how the year went.

festivals.name: First Leaf
festivals.description: The children choose and name the year's first new leaf, then argue about it until supper.

pride: Their spirits trust them. A grove the Aruvi tend never goes wild.

makersMarks: a leaf carved so finely it seems to move
a drop of red lacquer shaped like a seed
the maker's grove-sign burned into the grain

relations.note: Honey and lacquer for grain and cheese, with gentle lectures about trees included free.
They share the marsh-forest edge, and Moth Lantern Night and the Firefly Ferry are held on the same evening.
A polite, unending debate over whose tea is better.
